readerQuestion: How can I build one Home Assistant Sections dashboard that stays useful on a phone and a tablet without installing custom cards?
directAnswer: Create a separate dashboard from scratch with a Sections view. Start with Everyday, Rooms and Readings in that order, a maximum of two section columns, native Tile controls and an Entities readings list. Card full width means section width; small screens can use fewer columns. Verify icon versus body taps with a new unused Toggle helper before substituting one non-critical lamp. Hidden cards or tabs and a non-admin account do not establish room-only authorization.
originalContribution: The worked-layout section proposes a specific three-section household arrangement, explains why each item earns space, and defines success on both screen sizes. The rehearsal places the same harmless helper in a Tile and an Entities row and checks its state on two clients, distinguishing layout from actual commands. A six-row troubleshooting table separates section width, nested-card sizing, card selection, tap defaults and device communication.
limitations: Documentation research, not hardware testing or a tested Home Assistant installation. The room layout is illustrative; exact menu wording and responsive placement vary with installed release, screen width, sidebar and zoom. Browser verification covers the published article and library, not a running Home Assistant frontend. The cover is generated conceptual art, not a product photo. No device latency, compatibility measurement, ranking improvement or indexing outcome is claimed. Research-access limitations are recorded in the internal topic brief.
proofreadFixes: Added the explicit Create step after naming the dashboard. Replaced above the fold with on screen without scrolling and simplified section-column terminology. Verified the potentially consequential directions against official docs: Full width is scoped to the containing section; two sections wide is a maximum; nested stack/Grid cards and picture elements lack the Layout tab; a Tile body opens more-info while its icon toggles a toggleable entity by default. The practice helper remains unused by automations; security and heating devices are excluded from the first test. Confirmed visible authorship, four direct TLDR bullets, research disclosure and professional source labels. The first desktop screenshot caught the image before asynchronous decoding finished; a repeat capture after image.decode() showed the complete cover. Final automated editorial pass found no remaining clarity or technical corrections.

claimChecks.claim: A new dashboard can be created from scratch through Settings > Dashboards, leaving the generated dashboard available. Menu wording depends on installed release.
Max number of sections wide limits section columns; dense placement can fill gaps around wider sections and affect visual order.
Sections adapt the number of section columns to available width; cards live in a separate grid inside each section. Two columns are not guaranteed on a narrow screen.
Cards can be added by card type. Full width card fills a section; the Layout tab is unavailable inside horizontal/vertical stacks or Grid cards and on picture elements cards.
The native Entities card lists multiple entities and its header toggle can operate all eligible entities; use sensors for the readings example and disable the header toggle when shown.
Tile body tap defaults to more-info; icon tap defaults to toggling a toggleable entity, otherwise more-info. These are independent configurable actions.

A Toggle helper stores a virtual on/off state and can trigger automations. The rehearsal therefore requires a new unused helper and checking that broad rules do not act on it; no physical safety control is exercised.
Conversion to Sections creates an additional view and retains the original. The documented migration tool does not support converting Sections back to another view type.
Hiding a view only hides its tab; the URL remains accessible. Visibility must not be presented as room-only access control.
Authorization is a server-side permission check. A non-admin account combined with hidden cards or tabs is not evidence of entity-specific access restriction.
